title: Research Assistant / Part-time Research Assistant
department: Department of Food Science and Nutrition
project: Mindfulness-based eating awareness training (MB-EAT) intervention for patients with diabetes and obesity: a randomized controlled trial
summary:
- University: Hong Kong Polytechnic University
- Department: Department of Food Science and Nutrition
- Project: Mindfulness-based eating awareness training (MB-EAT) intervention for patients with diabetes and obesity: a randomized controlled trial
- Duties: The appointees will assist the project leader in the research project - “Mindfulness-based eating awareness training (MB-EAT) intervention for patients with diabetes and obesity: a randomized controlled trial”. In this project, the research team aims to investigate (i) the efficacy of a 10-week MB-EAT intervention on anthropometric measures in adults with diabetes and obesity; and (ii) the efficacy of a 10-week MB-EAT intervention in terms of glycaemic control, eating behaviour, psychological health, and hormones regulating stress and appetite. The appointees will be required to (a) assist in data collection and processing, and preliminary reporting of results; (b) assist in chemical analysis of biological samples; and (c) perform any other duties as assigned by the project leader or his/her delegates.
- Requirements: Applicants should (a) have a bachelor’s degree in Health, Biology, Chemistry or a related discipline or an equivalent qualification; (b) have a good command of both written and spoken English and Chinese; (c) have good communication and interpersonal skills; (d) have a strong sense of responsibility; and (e) be self-motivated and able to work independently. Preference will be given to those with at least one year of research/relevant work experience.
- Appointment: (1) Research Assistant (one to two post(s)): each for six months initially, with possibility of further appointment; (2) Part-time Research Assistant (one to two post(s)): each for six months initially, with possibility of further appointment
- Conditions: For full-time appointment(s), a highly competitive remuneration package will be offered. For part-time appointment(s), the remuneration rate is HK$125 per hour. Consideration of applications will commence on 21 October 2026 until the positions are filled.
- Contact: Applicants are invited to contact Prof. Lo Ka Hei Kenneth via email at kenneth.kh.lo@polyu.edu.hk for further information.
- Closing date: 2026-10-21

title: Postdoctoral Fellow / Research Associate / Research Assistant
project: Intelligent thermal spraying system for high performance coatings (ITSS HPC)
summary:
- University: Hong Kong Polytechnic University
- Department: Aviation Services Research Centre
- Project: Intelligent thermal spraying system for high performance coatings (ITSS HPC)
- Duties: The appointees will assist the project leader in the research project - “Intelligent thermal spraying system for high performance coatings (ITSS HPC)”. This project is a collaborative initiative with Hong Kong Aircraft Engineering Company Limited (HAECO), Hong Kong Aero Engine Services Limited (HAESL), and The Boeing Company. The project aims to design and develop an intelligent, automated, and integrated thermal spraying system to significantly improve coating performance for aero engines and other high performance applications. The system will reduce maintenance time by 40%, cut oxygen and fuel consumption by 50%, and lower overall costs by 30% through reductions in waste and rework. Multi sensor fusion and material modification technologies will ensure coatings with superior wear, corrosion, and high temperature resistance. Research activities will be conducted in the Centre’s laboratories and workshops under the University’s collaborative agreements with industry sponsors. The appointees will be required to (a) apply design and systems engineering principles to develop automated spraying processes; (b) support design and prototyping of intelligent HVOF spraying equipment with integrated control systems; (c) contribute to the development of multi sensor fusion technologies for defect prediction and process parameter adjustment; (d) assist in material modification research to enhance coating density, adhesion, and reduce substrate thermal deformation; (e) develop and validate robotic spray path generation using 3D scanning; (f) implement energy management strategies to optimise fuel and oxygen usage; (g) collaborate with industrial partners and academic supervisors to ensure deliverables align with sponsor requirements and Innovation and Technology Commission compliance; (h) generate engineering documentation, inspection records, and process databases; and (i) perform any other duties as assigned by the project leader or his/her delegate(s).
- Requirements: Applicants for the Postdoctoral Fellow post should have a doctoral degree or an equivalent qualification and must have no more than five years of post-qualification experience at the time of application. Applicants for the Research Associate post should have a master’s degree or a good honours degree with three years of research / relevant work experience. Applicants for the Research Assistant post should have an honours degree or an equivalent qualification, with research / relevant work experience being an advantage. For all posts, applicants should have (a) an interest in working in the aviation sector, non-destructive inspection, robotics, automation, data analytics, and test specimen analysis via universal testing methods and coating technologies; and (b) a good command of written and spoken English. The following skills and experience are beneficial but not mandatory (a) a strong background in robotics, mechatronics, or mechanical systems design; (b) experience with non-destructive testing (NDT) methods (e.g. ultrasonic, thermography, eddy current); (c) knowledge of automation, control systems, and sensor integration; (d) familiarity with AI/machine learning for defect detection or image analysis; (e) proficiency in CAD/CAE tools and engineering documentation standards; (f) hands-on experience in laboratory prototyping, testing, and data analysis; and (g) the ability to work in multi-disciplinary, sponsor-driven environments with compliance and reporting requirements.
- Appointment: (2) Research Associate / Research Assistant (two posts): each for twelve to twenty-four months
- Conditions: A highly competitive remuneration package will be offered. Consideration of applications will commence on 25 September 2026 until the positions are filled.
- Contact: Applicants are invited to contact Mr Robert Voyle at telephone number 3400 3504 or via email at robert.voyle@polyu.edu.hk for further information.
- Closing date: 2026-09-25

title: Postdoctoral Fellow / Research Associate / Research Assistant
project: Airframe Inspection via Robotic Continuum Induction Thermography (AIRCIT)
summary:
- University: Hong Kong Polytechnic University
- Department: Aviation Services Research Centre
- Project: Airframe Inspection via Robotic Continuum Induction Thermography (AIRCIT)
- Duties: The appointees will assist the project leader in the research project - “Airframe Inspection via Robotic Continuum Induction Thermography (AIRCIT)”. This project addresses one of aviation’s most hazardous and labour-intensive tasks: fuel tank and confined-space inspections. By integrating continuum robotics, induction thermography, and automated defect recording, AIRCIT aims to reduce inspection time by up to 70%, enhance worker safety, and deliver validated outcomes for industry partners including HAECO, HAESL, and Boeing. Research activities will be conducted in ASRC’s fabrication facilities, laboratories, and workshops, under the University’s collaborative agreements with industry sponsors. The appointees will be required to (a) apply sound design and systems engineering principles to develop automated processes; (b) support design and prototyping of continuum robots with enhanced payload and reach for confined-space inspection; (c) contribute to the development of lightweight induction thermography heads and vision systems for crack detection beneath sealant; (d) support the development of innovative techniques in continuum robot path planning for surface inspection processes; (e) assist in implementing TRACE (Tracking and Recording of Anomalies in Component Evaluation) using RFID tagging and location marking systems; (f) work with industrial partners and departmental professors to ensure deliverables align with sponsor requirements and funding compliance; (g) generate engineering documentation in accordance with the Centre’s procedures for data development and evaluation; and (h) perform any other duties as assigned by the project leader or his/her delegate(s).
- Requirements: Applicants for the Postdoctoral Fellow post should have a doctoral degree or an equivalent qualification and must have no more than five years of post-qualification experience at the time of application. Applicants for the Research Associate post should have a master’s degree or a good honours degree with three years of research / relevant work experience. Applicants for the Research Assistant post should have an honours degree or an equivalent qualification, with research / relevant work experience being an advantage. For all posts, applicants should have (a) interest in working in the aviation sector, non-destructive inspection, robotics, automation, data analytics, and test specimen analysis via universal testing methods such as ultrasonic test or induction thermography; and (b) a good command of written and spoken English. The following skills and experience are beneficial but not mandatory (a) strong background in robotics, mechatronics, or mechanical systems design; (b) experience with non-destructive testing (NDT) methods (e.g., ultrasonic, thermography, eddy current); (c) knowledge of automation, control systems, and sensor integration; (d) familiarity with AI/machine learning for defect detection or image analysis; (e) proficiency in CAD/CAE tools and engineering documentation standards; (f) hands-on experience in laboratory prototyping, testing, and data analysis; and (g) ability to work in multi-disciplinary, sponsor-driven environments with compliance and reporting requirements.
- Appointment: (2) Research Associate / Research Assistant (two posts): each for twelve to twenty-four months
- Conditions: A highly competitive remuneration package will be offered. Consideration of applications will commence on 24 June 2026 until the positions are filled.
